newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaican tourism minister quits after gun fracas.
newsitem.headline: Jamaican tourism minister quits after gun fracas.

text.p: Jamaican tourism minister John Junor resigned on Tuesday following a March 20 incident in which he fired his gun during a political confrontation in his constituency.
"I sincerely regret having brought into scrutiny my own recent response to the disgusting and indecent attack on me," Junor said in a letter to Prime Minister P.J. Patterson.
Patterson accepted Junor's resignation but said: "We cannot seek to countenance vile abuse or seek political capital by supporting unwarranted political attacks."

Witnesses said Junor exchanged angry words with a heckler and then threw the first punch as the two exchanged blows. During the confrontation, the minister went to his vehicle and discharged his gun, which was licensed, into the air.

Junor said he felt he was justified in his actions, as he had been "subject to abuse in the extreme." He also received expressions of support from his constituency in central Jamaica and the ruling Peoples National Party.

But Junor was criticised for actions that could endanger the image of Jamaica's tourism industry, already grappling with the island's high violent crime rate. There were 920 murders in Jamaica in 1996.
The opposition Jamaica Labour Party called repeatedly for Junor's resignation.
Police have not determined if Junor will face charges. It is illegal in Jamaica to discharge a firearm near a public road or in large gatherings without just cause.

Junor was named tourism minister in January 1992 by then prime minister Michael Manley. He was made local government minister in 1993 when Patterson succeeded Manley, but returned to tourism during a cabinet reshuffle in January 1995.
